slides.title: Rising churn is an SMB problem: SMB accounts for 96% of the extra customers we now lose each month

claims.claim: Rising churn is an SMB problem: SMB accounts for 96% of the extra customers we now lose each month
evidence: Monthly logo churn H1 2025 → H1 2026: SMB 2.0% → 3.1%; Mid-market 0.6% → 0.8%; Enterprise 0.2% → 0.2%
SMB share of the extra customers lost each month: 96% = 5,900 × 1.1 pp ÷ (5,900 × 1.1 pp + 1,350 × 0.2 pp)

claims.claim: The rise is SMB logos; mid-market matters more in dollars
evidence: SMB share of the extra ARR lost each month: 74% = $21.0M × 1.1 pp ÷ ($21.0M × 1.1 pp + $41.0M × 0.2 pp)

claims.claim: SMB: the only jump, so something changed in SMB in 2025
Mid-market: a small rise on our largest ARR base; watch renewals
The board dashboard's undefined "1.4% → 2.3%" matches neither the customer-weighted (1.7% → 2.6%) nor the ARR-weighted (0.8% → 1.2%) average of this table; it is not used

slides.title: The 2025 promotion, not a broad SMB exodus, explains 91% of the rise in SMB churn

claims.claim: 91% of the 1.1 percentage point rise in SMB monthly churn comes from the promotion cohort
evidence: SMB H1 2025 2.0%; Other SMB customers +0.1 pp; Promotion cohort +1.0 pp; SMB H1 2026 3.1%
Promotion cohort step = SMB churn minus churn of SMB customers who did not come through the promotion (3.1% − 2.1%); those customers churned 2.0% in H1 2025, the same as all SMB

claims.claim: Other SMB customers: churn moved only 0.1 percentage points, so the base paying full price has not turned on us
Promotion cohort: 2,100 customers, 36% of SMB, who joined at half price in 2025 and carry $4.4M of ARR
evidence: Promotion: 50% off the first six months for new self-serve SMB customers, February to August 2025

claims.claim: Timing: most who left did so within two months of their discount ending

slides.title: Promotion customers never set the product up and left over price once their discount ended

claims.claim: Only 41% of promotion customers got started in their first month, against 72% of others
evidence: New customers sending at least five documents in month one: Promotion cohort 41%; Other cohorts 72%

claims.claim: Price complaints come from the promotion cohort; other SMB churners cite price as often as in 2025
evidence: SMB churners citing price or a cheaper option: Promotion cohort H1 2026 52%; All SMB H1 2026 34%; All SMB H1 2025 19%; Other SMB H1 2026 18%

claims.claim: Activation, not price, is the lever: low-activity new customers churn about three times as often
Most promotion-cohort customers who left did so within two months of the discount ending

slides.title: The CFO's plan is worth at most $7.6M in 2027, not $10.3M, because nearly a quarter of ARR does not renew

claims.claim: The CFO's plan is worth at most $7.6M in 2027, not $10.3M, because nearly a quarter of ARR does not renew
evidence: 12% on all ARR (CFO) $10.32M; Mid-market renewing after 2027 −$0.738M; Enterprise renewing after 2027 −$1.728M; Enterprise 7% caps −$0.288M; Reachable in 2027 $7.566M
$65.5M ARR renewing in 2027 × 12% CFO's list-price rise − $0.3M lost to 7% enterprise caps = $7.6M reachable, before churn
CFO: "Raise list prices 12% on every plan at renewal from January 2027. That is $10.3M of ARR"; $86.0M × 12% = $10.3M

claims.claim: Renewal timing: 15% of mid-market and 60% of enterprise ARR renew after 2027, beyond the plan's reach
Caps: 60% of enterprise ARR cannot rise more than 7% a year by contract
A third of what is left sits in the churning segment
evidence: SMB share of the reachable uplift 33% = $21.0M × 12% ÷ $7.6M

claims.claim: Share of the $12.9M growth target covered 59%

slides.title: In SMB, the CFO's rise would widen the gap to Inkwell just as our win rate against it fell to 38%

claims.claim: At $16.80, our SMB plan would cost nearly twice Inkwell's Starter plan
evidence: List price $/user/month: Inkwell Starter 9; Palisade SMB today 15; Palisade SMB after +12% 16.8; Inkwell Pro 24; Palisade Business 29

claims.claim: We already lose most SMB deals where Inkwell is in the running
evidence: −13 pp
Palisade win rate in SMB deals where Inkwell was considered: H1 2025 51%; H1 2026 38%
Inkwell launched its $9 Starter plan in October 2025, between the two win-rate readings

claims.claim: Inkwell has not been seen in mid-market or enterprise deals with more than 200 seats

slides.title: Even the milder 2023 SMB rise of 8% lifted churn for six months and left it higher than before

claims.claim: Even the milder 2023 SMB rise of 8% lifted churn for six months and left it higher than before
evidence: SMB price rise at renewal, 2023: 8% (two-thirds of the 12% now proposed)
SMB monthly churn before the rise: 1.8%
SMB monthly churn for six months after: 2.3% (0.5 percentage points above the start)
SMB monthly churn once it settled: 1.9% (never back to the starting point)

claims.claim: Repeated on today's $21.0M SMB ARR: 0.5 percentage points × six months ≈ $0.6M lost
evidence: $0.6M is our estimate: $21.0M × 0.5 percentage points × 6 months, assuming lost customers carry average SMB ARR

claims.claim: Today's base is already at 3.1%, with Inkwell now in the market
The core tolerated the rise, and non-promotion churners cite price no more than before (18%)
So SMB needs a measured test, not a freeze and not a blind 12%

slides.title: Mid-market and enterprise can carry a price rise: both expand revenue from existing customers and barely churn

claims.claim: Mid-market and enterprise can carry a price rise: both expand revenue from existing customers and barely churn
evidence: SMB: ARR $21M; NRR 94%; monthly churn H1 2026 3.1%; change +1.1 pp; 2027 move: Hold in January: churn up, NRR below 100%
Mid-market: ARR $41M; NRR 112%; churn 0.8%; change 0.2 pp; 2027 move: Raise 10% at renewal / Largest prize: 48% of ARR, 85% of it renewing in 2027
Enterprise: ARR $24M; NRR 118%; churn 0.2%; change 0 pp; 2027 move: Raise within contract caps

claims.claim: Customer advisory board (2026): integrations and the audit trail are the main reasons mid-market and enterprise customers stay; Inkwell has not been seen in deals above 200 seats

slides.title: A 10% higher price did not measurably slow mid-market sign-ups in 2024, making it the tested level for renewals

claims.claim: A 10% higher price did not measurably slow mid-market sign-ups in 2024
evidence: 10% higher list price for new mid-market sign-ups
23.1% conversion at the higher price
23.6% conversion in the control group at the old price
Half a percentage point below the control group; Not statistically significant

claims.claim: The rise we recommend for mid-market renewals in 2027; Below the CFO's 12%, which no test has covered
Renewals are not sign-ups, but customers who stay for integrations and the audit trail face real switching costs at renewal
evidence: Customer advisory board, 2026

slides.title: Mid-market and enterprise renewals alone would add about $4.3M of ARR in 2027 at tested price levels

claims.claim: Mid-market and enterprise renewals alone would add about $4.3M of ARR in 2027 at tested price levels
evidence: $3.5M mid-market: $34.9M renewing in 2027 (85% of $41.0M) × 10%, the 2024 test level
$0.4M enterprise without caps: $3.8M renewing × 10%
$0.4M enterprise with caps: $5.8M renewing × the 7% cap
= $4.3M ARR added by December 2027, before any churn effect and before SMB

claims.claim: SMB is left out: if the 2027 test passes, 8% on the $16.6M of non-promotion SMB ARR adds up to $1.3M

slides.title: A targeted rise beats both alternatives, claiming tested value while sparing churning SMB customers a January increase

evidence: A · 12% on every plan (CFO): 59% of growth target; $21M SMB ARR facing January rise; 12% untested, 2023 SMB rise of 8% lifted churn; High NRR risk; Overstates the prize, risks SMB
B · Targeted by segment: 33%; None, a test sample only; Mid-market 10% tested in 2024, caps honored; Low risk; Recommended / Plus up to $1.3M once the SMB test passes
C · Hold all prices: None; None; No price risk, tested value unclaimed; None from price, SMB's 94% still drags; Leaves value on the table

normalized.recommendation: Raise prices in 2027 by segment: mid-market and enterprise from January, SMB only after a test and once the promotion cohort is activated. Raise mid-market and enterprise from January for about $4.3M (mid-market +10% at renewal, enterprise within contract caps); decide SMB on a test by mid-2027 (8% renewal test against a holdout, go/no-go at the end of Q2 2027); price the promotion cohort only once activated; plan on the cohort fix, not the halving.

alternatives_considered.treatment: Rejected: "Overstates the prize, risks SMB". Worth at most $7.6M, not $10.3M (59% of growth target); $21M SMB ARR faces a January rise; 12% untested and the 2023 SMB rise of 8% lifted churn; High risk to NRR: the full rise hits SMB, already at 94%.

Recommended: 33% of growth target; no SMB ARR faces a January rise (test sample only); mid-market 10% tested in 2024, caps honored; Low NRR risk: rises only where NRR is 112–118%. Plus up to $1.3M once the SMB test passes. Gives up $3.3M vs. CFO plan before churn.
Rejected: "Leaves value on the table". No price risk; tested value unclaimed; SMB's 94% still drags.

alternatives_considered.option: SMB freeze vs. blind 12% vs. measured test
alternatives_considered.treatment: "SMB needs a measured test, not a freeze and not a blind 12%".

alternatives_considered.option: Customer Success onboarding programme halving SMB churn
alternatives_considered.treatment: "Plan on the cohort fix, not the halving"; halving needs a rate below any in the pack; no evidence for the halving was in the briefing pack. Cohort fix could cut SMB churn by about a third (32%).

assumptions_and_uncertainties: Synthetic benchmark data; every number from the briefing pack

The board dashboard's undefined "1.4% → 2.3%" matches neither the customer-weighted nor the ARR-weighted average; it is not used
Exit-survey shares cover churned customers who answered the survey; sample sizes were not in the briefing pack
$0.6M is our estimate: $21.0M × 0.5 percentage points × 6 months, assuming lost customers carry average SMB ARR
Whether new sign-ups predict renewal behavior is an open question, so the rollout carries a churn guardrail

85% of mid-market and 40% of enterprise ARR renew in 2027, as the renewal calendar shows
The 7% caps cover 60% of renewing enterprise ARR, the same share as the whole enterprise book
No extra churn from the rise is netted out; a guardrail pauses the rise if renewed accounts churn faster
SMB is left out: if the 2027 test passes, 8% on the $16.6M of non-promotion SMB ARR adds up to $1.3M
Pricing alone cannot deliver the $12.9M growth objective under any option; new business and SMB retention must carry the rest
Customer Success halving claim: no evidence for the halving was in the briefing pack
Guardrail: pause if renewed accounts churn above H1 2026 levels (mid-market: 0.8% a month)

normalized.extraction_notes: The deck had no pictures; every chart came through as series data and I converted the values to percentages. On slide 2, I used the executive summary's headline sentence as the governing thought and listed the numbered points and sub-bullets below it in order. Slide 8's waterfall chart shows $10.32M less $0.738M, $1.728M and $0.288M, which leaves $7.566M. The deck doesn't spell out which segment the $0.288M cap deduction comes from beyond calling it "Enterprise 7% caps". Two figures are stated differently in different places: slide 16 calls the growth target "15%" in a table header and "$12.9M" in a footnote, and slide 8 links the two as $86.0M × 15%. I recorded both as written.
